svg.text: The radio is a USB device in its own right. No serial adapter, no chip, just wire.
RJ45 plug — contact side, as it goes into the radio
Pin 7 is an output — the radio supplies 5 V there. Leave it unconnected.
Joining it to the computer's 5 V ties two supplies together with nothing between
them. Worse, pin 7 sits next to pin 6, so a slip puts 5 V onto a 3.6 V data line.
Contacts toward you, latch behind, nose pointing into the radio: pin 1 on the left — the same
order you see looking into the jack. Turn the plug over and it reverses, so count the pins.
Wire colours are the USB convention and usually hold — check with a meter before you cut.
